sentences.text: Coram:

Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Saurabh Banerjee
 Order

The petitioners vide the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973 seek quashing of FIR No.105/2019 dated 06.04.2019 registered under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC at P.S: R.K. Puram, Delhi and all proceeding emanating therefrom in view of the Compromise Deed/Memorandum of Understanding dated 03.09.2022 arrived at between the parties.

2. This petition is accompanied by the Compromise Deed/ Memorandum of Understanding dated 03.09.2022 [Annexure-P-2] and is also supported by affidavits of all the petitioners and of respondent no.2, alongwith proofs of their respective I.Ds.
CRL.M.C. 8343/2023 page 1 of 3 This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 11/11/2023 at 10:38:15 3.
Petitioner nos.1 to 4 as also respondent no.2 are present in Court and have been identified by the IO.
Their credentials have been verified by this Court.
4. Issue Notice.
5. Learned APP for the State accepts notice.
He confirms that he has no objection to the quashing of the FIR.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent no.2 also accepts notice.
Respondent no.2 confirms that the petitioner no.1 and respondent no.2 have been granted divorce by mutual consent vide Decree of Divorce dated 17.04.2018.

She further affirms the Compromise Deed/Memorandum of Understanding dated 03.09.2022 whereby she has already received the total sum of Rs.30,00,000/-
in full and final settlement of all her claims including alimony, maintenance (present, past and future), stridhan etc.
She states that she has no objection to the quashing of the present FIR.

7. In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties and following the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jitendra Raghuvanshi & Ors. Vs. Babita Raguvanshi & Anr (2013) 4 SCC 58, Gian Singh vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2012) 10 SCC 303 and Narinder Singh & Ors. vs. State of Punjab & Anr. (2014) 6 SCC 466, this Court is of the opinion that continuation of the aforesaid FIR will be an exercise in futility.

Tarun Gokul vis-a-vis his parents, as may be available under law, in any manner whatsoever.
10. The petition alongwith the pending application stands disposed of.
